caption:
बॉलीवुड की चकाचौंध से दूर गोवा में बच्चों की परवरिश कर रहीं समीरा रेड्डी ने एक इंटरव्यू में कई बड़े खुलासे किए हैं!

समीरा ने संजय दत्त की फिल्म Aakhri Sawal से कमबैक किया है। उन्होंने बताया कि संजय दत्त ने उनके लिए खास इंतजाम किया, जिससे वह 2-3 महीने तक सिर्फ weekend पर शूटिंग कर सकीं और बाकी दिन गोवा में बच्चों के साथ रहीं। 🎬

साउथ सिनेमा के बड़े स्टार्स जैसे Chiranjeevi, Jr NTR, Suriya, Ajith और Mohanlal के साथ काम कर चुकीं समीरा का कहना है कि साउथ ने उन्हें बॉलीवुड से कहीं ज्यादा इज्जत, पैसा और स्टारडम दिया है। 🌟

न्यू मदर्स के काम के घंटों पर बात करते हुए समीरा ने कहा कि ब्रेस्टफीडिंग और काम संभालना मुश्किल है, लेकिन प्रोड्यूसर्स का भारी पैसा भी लगा होता है, इसलिए दोनों पक्षों की बात समझनी चाहिए। 💭

अगले महीने 48 साल की होने जा रही समीरा ने कहा कि social media पर अपने सफेद बाल और बढ़ा वजन दिखाना उनकी मेंटल हेल्थ के लिए राहत भरा है।

क्या आपको भी लगता है कि साउथ सिनेमा बॉलीवुड से ज्यादा अपने स्टार्स की कद्र करता है? कमेंट्स में जरूर बताइए! 👇

ctx.title: Sameera Reddy says South cinema gave her far more respect, money and stardom than Bollywood | Interview
ctx.summary: Sameera Reddy shared her take on the debate around working hours for new mothers in films and reflected on her experience in South Indian cinema.
ctx.text:
Sameera Reddy stepped away from films for several years to focus on raising her two children in Goa. She recently made her comeback with Sanjay Dutt's Aakhri Sawal , but thanks to her candid and relatable presence on social media, it feels like she has never really been away.
In a conversation with Hindustan Times, the actor opened up about returning to films and how Sanjay accommodated her schedule, allowing her to shoot over weekends so she could be with her children during the week. She also shared her take on the debate around working hours for new mothers, and reflected on why her experience in South Indian cinema has been far more rewarding than her stint in Bollywood. Read on:
It was wonderful. Having done two or three films with Sanjay earlier, reuniting felt very comfortable. Sanjay also produced this film and he was extremely sweet. The main reason I haven’t done feature films or OTT projects over the past few years is that I am a very hands-on mother living in Goa. My life from morning to night revolves around my kids, and I found it very hard to leave them for weeks to shoot on set. But Sanjay accommodated me by suggesting, “Just come and shoot on the weekends.” Because of that arrangement, I shot every weekend over two to three months and loved every bit of it.
When I shot for Sanjay’s film, I shot continuously and didn’t mind the long hours or extra shifts at all because I wanted to finish the work efficiently for my producer, especially since I don’t live in Mumbai. But I have done extra shifts when the need of the hour.
That being said, being a new mother comes with immense pressure — managing breastfeeding, hormonal changes and work simultaneously is not easy. If a producer can adjust and accommodate that actor...it is a two way street. But if it doesn't work for the producer than everybody has to understand it. Looking at it from a producer’s perspective, massive daily financial investments are riding on a film set, and delays can be very costly.
Both sides of the situation need to be recognized and respected. While I cannot comment directly on Deepika Padukone’s specific stance, but I understand, she is an amazing actor and if that was she needs, that is what she needs. But you can't have a one-sided view on this.
To be completely honest, I had a superb experience in South Indian cinema. I worked with top stars including Chiranjeevi, Jr NTR, Suriya, Ajith, and Mohanlal, and my personal experiences were wonderful. Everyone’s journey is different, but for me, my Southern film experience was way above my experience in Bollywood.
The respect, artistic value, financial compensation, and stardom I received in the South far surpassed what I experienced in Hindi cinema. Even today, 18 years later, the love and respect I receive from my Southern fans is unprecedented. While a Bollywood fan might say, “Oh yeah, there was a Sameera Reddy,” fans in the South still greet me warmly, saying, “We love you. You are our Meghna from Vaaranam Aayiram!” I will always hold the softest corner in my heart for my South Indian films, and in my mind, I will always consider myself a South Indian actor first.
Responsibility? God no, it is a relief. Showing my real self — whether it’s grey hair, stretch marks, weight fluctuations, or hormonal breakouts — gives me better mental health. It allows me to wake up and simply be myself every day. Over the six years I’ve been on social media, I have stayed true to this journey and built a safe community for women. Turning 48 next month, I intend to celebrate it proudly out loud.
Vibha Maru is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times Entertainment, based in Delhi. With a decade of experience across digital and print media, she covers Bollywood, Hollywood and web shows.
